note: Harrison County Conservation Board park between Woodbine and Dunlap, two miles off Highway 30 on a gravel road, with an electric-motor fishing lake, boat ramp and pier. Pads sit on a bench above the water behind the loop road. --Claude
summary: County page confirms 20/30 amp, $25, first-come, Apr-Oct; count 15->12 RV sites; pond lead down.
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD (pond -> not waterfront, unsure so going down; I changed nothing; lakeview if AWH takes the county's acreage): a road runs between pads and water, and the pier stems from it, so on-water fails (own loop road). The earlier evidence said 'open apron, no buffer', which the imagery contradicts. Pads about 25-40 m from the shore, unobstructed view. Size decides the rest: the county says 'six-acre fishing lake' and imagery scales it at about 3-4 acres (dark, low-contrast frame). At over 5 acres it follows the local name, lake, and lakeview fits. Under 5 it's a pond, with no pond-view value.

HOOKUPS: 'electricity (20 and 30 amp) and water hydrants' doesn't say whether a hydrant serves each site or a few are shared. Stored water true left alone; if shared it should be false with potable_water true. Campsite photos or the county would settle it.
BOOKING: earlier evidence mentioned RV 'book-now'. The county's facility page says no reservations, even though the site's template shows an Availability link. Stored first-come stands.
